## Verdict: request changes, don't block

The finding that matches the PR is `crime_00017`, `dst_naive_arithmetic` — charge **"DST-Naive Day Math"**, `severity: medium`, `confidence: 0.8`, `src/date.ts:52`. Its evidence, verbatim:

> - `"+ 86400000 (day) @L52"`
> - `"lines: 52"`
> - `"use a calendar-aware library (Luxon, Temporal, date-fns-tz) for day math"`

and the summary:

> `"1 day-level millisecond constant in arithmetic. A day isn't 86,400,000 ms on DST-transition days; manual ms math drifts silently."`

**Why request-changes rather than block.** The finding is `medium`/0.8, not `high`/0.95 — and correctly so, because `+86400000` is *exactly right* if `tomorrowMs` is only ever treated as "24 hours from this instant." It's wrong only when the result is read back as a wall-clock calendar day. The detector can't see which of those the callers do, hence 0.8. `effort: "medium"`, `fix_shape: "use a DST-aware library; never add seconds to a wall-clock date"` — this is a small, well-scoped change, not a redesign.

**What pushes it past "nit"** is the rest of the file. `crime_00009` (**"Half-UTC, Half-Local"**, `severity: high`) reports:

> `"\"d\" uses getUTCFullYear() @L9 and getMonth() @L41"`

so this module demonstrably mixes the two time domains already — meaning the assumption that `tomorrowMs`'s output stays a pure instant is not one this file has earned. `crime_00011` (**"Timezone Roulette"**, `"unsafe literals: \"2026-12-25T07:00:00\", \"2026-12-20\""`) says the same thing from the input side. That's the argument to make in the PR: the helper isn't wrong in isolation, it's wrong in this neighbourhood.

I'd hard-block only if `tomorrowMs` feeds a billing or entitlement boundary (trial expiry, dunning, invoice period) — a one-day slip there is a customer-visible charge, and `src/billing.ts` is in the same repo.

## The two dates per year

The two **DST transition days in the host runtime's zone** — the only two days that aren't 86,400,000 ms long. Which calendar dates those are depends on the zone, e.g.:

| Zone | Spring forward (23 h day) | Fall back (25 h day) |
|---|---|---|
| US (`America/New_York` etc.) | 2nd Sunday in March | 1st Sunday in November |
| EU (`Europe/London` etc.) | last Sunday in March | last Sunday in October |

How each one fails:

- **Spring forward** — the local day is 23 h. Adding 24 h overshoots by an hour: same wall time on day D becomes *one hour later* on D+1 (09:00 → 10:00). Correct calendar day, wrong wall clock.
- **Fall back** — the local day is 25 h. Adding 24 h undershoots: local midnight on day D + 86,400,000 ms lands at **23:00 on day D**. "Tomorrow" is still today. This is the one that produces a wrong *date*, not just a wrong time — and the one that breaks any downstream `getDate()`/day-boundary comparison.

Note the scan output is the full-repo report (42 findings, `"report_type": "scan"`), not a file-scoped one — the `src/date.ts` subset is `crime_00001`, `00009`, `00011`, `00017`, `00026`, `00027`.

## Ask on the PR

Replace the ms arithmetic with a zone-aware `addDays`, per the finding's own `suggested_actions`:

> `"Replace ms-arithmetic with a timezone-aware addDays/subtract operation that knows about DST and leap years."`

And add a test pinned to the fall-back date in a DST zone — that's the case that returns the wrong day, and `test_gap: 0.5` says nothing currently covers it.
